summary: Researched on the morning of Tue 24 Nov; lineups are not out, so this is a draft until the final check. A Champions League night (matchday 5) plus DEL, Liiga and KHL hockey and Dota 2 BLAST Slam seeding matches; basketball is not researched (the owner's permanent rule). Medium: Como (DraftKings 75.8%), Betis at Slovan (DraftKings 76.2%), Leipzig (ClubElo, Bet365 and DraftKings near 70%), Bodø/Glimt (books and a model near 65%, title race live), Porto at Feyenoord (DraftKings, Kalshi and ClubElo near 44%) and Eisbären Berlin (1st v last; goalie unconfirmed). Low: Man City (two models about 20 points under the market, winless in four league games), Arsenal (Raya, Saka and Zubimendi out against an in-form Dortmund), Real Madrid (key facts rest on one thin preview), the KHL games Traktor and Metallurg, Ilves, Kölner Haie (goalies unconfirmed, thin markets, no second price for some) and the Dota 2 seeding matches (no second price; Yandex's price fell 3.9% with no news). Excluded: Galatasaray v Aston Villa (pitch problem at Rams Park). Views that contradicted a game's own main risk were dropped (over 2.5 goals for Betis, Como, Leipzig, Bodø and Porto; Man City goals views).

checks.team_news: Only one preview page (footballpredictions.com) lists absences. Real Madrid: Asencio, F. Mendy and Rodrygo out. PSV: Nagalo, Ouaissa, Plea and Schouten out, Mauro Junior doubtful. I found no club or press-conference confirmation, and no coach-change check for either side.
checks.lineups: Not out yet. Squawka predicts a 4-2-3-1 with Courtois, Mbappe up front, and Bellingham and Vinicius behind him. Footballpredictions expects Cucurella, Valverde and Vinicius back in the XI. Only one independent predicted-XI source and no PSV XI, so unverified. Official XIs come about an hour before kick-off.
checks.rotation: Not verified. I found no information on the previous or next Real Madrid league game, rest days or travel. Real Madrid beat AEK 3-2 away on 4 Nov and PSV lost 1-2 at home to Club Brugge that day, which suggests a full-strength Madrid side but is not confirmed.
checks.motivation: Footballpredictions (one source) has Real Madrid 2nd with 4 wins from 4 and PSV 24th on 4 points, so PSV need the result. Real Madrid cannot have secured their aim after matchday 4 of 8, so the hard rule does not apply. I could not check the official table, so this is not fully verified.
checks.form: Real Madrid have lost once in their last 10 in all competitions (2.70 points per game, 3.00 at home). They won 3-2 at AEK, which shows they conceded. PSV have 1.60 points per game over their last 10, and their last four games each had three or more goals. xG not found.
checks.h2h: No prior meeting data was found on the preview page. Style matchup is untested: Madrid heavy favourite at home, PSV leaky but able to score.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN: 1.13 / 10 / 16, opening 1.20 / 7.5 / 9.5, de-vigged home 0.844, draw 0.096, away 0.060 (total 4.5), source site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/soccer/uefa.champions/scoreboard?dates=20261124. This agrees with Polymarket home 0.846. The DraftKings line moved from 1.20 to 1.13 since opening, a shortening of the favourite, so no adverse drift. Polymarket 24h move: 0.835 to 0.845 (+1.2% relative), so no fall to explain. Polymarket volume was not checked. Footballpredictions lists Over 2.5 at 85% and BTTS at 65%.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating found. ClubElo and Opta were not checked, so this check is not met.
checks.venue_weather: Santiago Bernabeu, Madrid, a normal home venue. I found no weather or pitch information.

games.reason: The market and DraftKings agree at about 0.845 for a Real Madrid win and nothing in the news argues against it. But the table, injuries, lineups, rotation and a bookmaker-free model rest on one thin preview or are missing, so the check list is not clean enough for medium. Pre-mortem: the likely failure is a draw or an upset by an attacking PSV side that scores freely (four straight 3+ goal games). Madrid also conceded 2 at AEK. I found no evidence that either risk is reduced.
games.main_risk: A draw, or a PSV upset, in a high-scoring game. Madrid's defence leaks (2 conceded at AEK) and PSV have scored in recent games. Unverified: the official table, Madrid's weekend rotation, the coach situation and the model rating.

checks.team_news: Como: Kean out (tibia/shin, new setback), Addai, Diao and Jesus Rodriguez injured; Caqueret doubtful (muscular, UEFA); Chalobah fit; no suspensions (Sports Mole 22 Nov, UEFA predicted line-ups MD5, Goal/tips previews). AEK: Koita suspended (two-match ban after red card vs Real Madrid), Zubkov and Zine injured, Arriaga out (collarbone, UEFA); Varga back from a layoff. No coaching change reported for either side.
checks.lineups: Predicted, not confirmed (kick-off 20:00 UTC). Sports Mole: Como Butez; Couto, Chalobah, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas. UEFA: same XI with Yan Couto, Ramon, Chalobah, Valle at the back. AEK (Sports Mole): Brignoli; Rota, Moukoudi, Relvas, Pilios; Majer, Arriaga, Kairinen, Mantalos; Jovic, Varga. UEFA lists Strakosha in goal, Marin for Arriaga (out), so AEK's goalkeeper and midfield are unclear. No rotation reported for Como; this is its first-choice side minus the injured.
checks.rotation: Como's last league game was a 2-0 win over Cagliari; next game is Serie A home vs Juventus on Sun 29 Nov (ESPN schedule), so a little rotation or substitution management is possible but no source reports it. Como is at home, no travel. AEK last played a 0-0 draw at Kalamata (Greek competition) after the 3-2 loss to Real Madrid.
checks.motivation: League phase matchday 5 of 8: Como 4th with 9 points from 4 games (3 wins, 1 loss, 19 goals for, 6 against); a top-8 place is not yet secured, so Como still needs points. AEK 29th with 3 points (opening 1-0 win over LASK, then three defeats) and needs results to reach the play-off places. Not a hard-rule case: the favourite has not secured its aim. Fabregas said Como will stay with its attacking approach and called AEK a great team who made life hard for Real and Shakhtar.
checks.form: Como CL: 4-1 vs RB Leipzig, 3-2 loss at Feyenoord, 4-1 vs Man Utd, 9-1 at Lens; all competitions W W W W L W, seven wins in the last eight. AEK CL: L (3-2 vs Real Madrid), L, L, W (1-0 LASK); all competitions L W L L W D, latest 0-0 at Kalamata. AEK winless away in the Champions League.
checks.h2h: No previous senior meeting found (Sports Mole carries no head-to-head). Style: Como attack-minded and high-scoring, AEK leaky, so the main failure route is not a high-scoring game but a draw or one-goal win through chance conversion.
checks.odds: Polymarket: Como 78.4%, draw 13.3%, AEK 8.3% (event volume about $86.5k, win market about $52k; thin but active). Polymarket move 24h: Como 0.765 to 0.785 (+2.6% relative, rising, no drift against the favourite). DraftKings via ESPN (data.odds): 1.26 / 6.50 / 10.00, de-vigged 75.8 / 14.7 / 9.5, opening 1.31 / 5.75 / 7.00 (favourite shortened, no drift against). Other books: 1xBet 1.33 / 5.98 / 10.40 (rg.org), 1.37 / 5.36 / 9.90 (Completesports), 1.37 / 6.25 / 9.70 (bet-experts). Independent price agrees within about 3 points of Polymarket; the books' range implies about 70-76% for Como. DK total 3.5.
checks.models: ClubElo and World Football Elo not available (no data.rating, ClubElo API timed out). Bookmaker-free signals are only form and goal difference (Como +13 over four CL games vs AEK 3 points, 29th), model splits in previews: bet-experts 74 / 16 / 10, Completesports 64 / 20 / 16. No Elo check was possible, so the rating check is unverified.
checks.venue_weather: Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, Como, home venue, normal fixture; FotMob forecast about 6 C on the night, no extreme weather or pitch problem reported.

games.reason: Verified fixture (Como vs AEK Athens, CL league phase MD5, 24 Nov 20:00 UTC, no coach change). Como is a strong home favourite with a 9-1 and two 4-1 wins in this league phase, AEK has three defeats in four, and its suspended and injured players weaken the side. Second price (DraftKings de-vigged 75.8%) agrees with Polymarket within 3 points and the price has not fallen. I put p slightly below market because lineups are unconfirmed, Caqueret is doubtful, Kean and three wingers are out, there is a Juventus game on Sunday, no Elo rating could be read, and favourites around 70-80% have been priced slightly high.
games.main_risk: A draw or narrow result: Como without Kean and three wingers, with Caqueret doubtful and possible rotation before Juventus, fail to convert chances against an AEK that needs points and may sit deep. AEK also has a goalkeeper unclear (Brignoli or Strakosha) and no Elo cross-check was possible. For handicap -1.5 the likely failure is a one-goal win, so no view is given; AEK +3.5 and the team-goals legs also carry blow-out and single-goal risk so they get no view.

checks.team_news: Per the footballpredictions.com preview, Slovan are without Cerepkai (back) and Medvedev (calf), with Griger and Kianga off the roster and Camara doubtful. Betis are without Ceballos, Losada and Morante, and Antony is listed as doubtful in the table but 'should be fit' in the text. This is one source, and I found no Pellegrini press conference quote for this match. No suspensions found.
checks.lineups: Not out yet; official XIs come 60 minutes before kick-off. Predicted Betis XI (footballpredictions.com, Squawka): 4-2-3-1 with Vallés; Natan, Bellerín, Fran García, Bartra; Roca plus one; Antony, Fornals, Abde, Isco; Ruibal. Squawka also lists Llorente. Predicted Slovan XI: 3-4-2-1 with Macik; Wimmer, Tomanek, Pokorny; Mustafic, Ignatenko; Camara and Sporar. No sign of heavy rotation, but nothing is confirmed.
checks.rotation: Betis: no evidence of a rested side. They beat Elche 2-0 on 8 Nov. I could not confirm their next La Liga fixture, so weekend rotation is unverified. Slovan are at home with no travel burden.
checks.motivation: League-phase table before this game: Slovan 36th of 36 with 0 points from 4 and a 1:17 goal difference. Betis 11th with 9 points from 4 (3W, 1L, 8:6). Betis are inside the 9-24 play-off band and have not secured a top-8 place, so they still have something to play for. Slovan are close to eliminated. This is not a hard exclusion.
checks.form: Slovan lost all 4 league-phase games (1 goal scored, 17 conceded). Their last 10 in all competitions (per footballpredictions.com): 1.50 PPG, 2.33 goals conceded per game at home, xG 1.76 for and 1.50 against. Betis last 10: 2.00 PPG, 2.40 PPG at home and 1.60 away, 2.0 scored and 1.5 conceded per game, xG 1.88 for and 1.52 against. Betis' CL record: beat Lille 3-2, Porto 3-2 and Feyenoord 1-0, lost 2-1 at Dortmund. Their games are fairly open.
checks.h2h: No previous meetings found. Style matchup: Slovan are a bottom side who lose heavily. Betis' recent European games have been high-scoring, so a one-goal win is more likely than a rout.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN: home 10.5, draw 6.5, away 1.26 (opening away 1.29, so the favourite has shortened). De-vigged away 0.762, draw 0.147, home 0.091, total 3.5. Polymarket away is 0.7736, which agrees within 1.2 points. Polymarket 24h move: 0.785 to 0.775 (-1.3% relative), below the 3% threshold. Polymarket event volume is about 37.5k, with 25.4k on the Betis winner market, so it is moderately thin. footballpredictions.com lists Betis -1.5 AH at 60%, BTTS yes 59%, over 2.5 at 74%, and draw no bet Betis at 93%.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating obtained (ClubElo request timed out). The only model figure is Squawka's, with Betis at 47% in its preview (its comparison to a market figure was garbled), and the xG split above favours Betis only modestly. So the model check is incomplete and I am not leaning on it.
checks.venue_weather: Tehelné pole, Bratislava, 20:00 UK time (21:00 CET), the regular home ground. Referee J. Brisard (France). I found no weather or pitch problem reported, but I did not check a forecast.

games.reason: Betis are a clear favourite at a winless bottom side, and DraftKings (0.762 de-vigged) agrees with Polymarket (0.774). No hard rule applies: Slovan's coach Yaya Touré was appointed on 13 June, long past the 7-day window, and Betis still need points. Medium rather than high because lineups are unconfirmed, the team news comes from one preview, no Pellegrini press conference was found, the Elo check failed, and Betis' next fixture is unknown. I trimmed p slightly below the market for the draw and rotation risks.
games.main_risk: A draw or one-goal result: Betis win by only a goal in an open game, concede on a set piece, or ease off or rotate ahead of a league game. Antony is doubtful and Betis are missing three squad players. Slovan have scored once in four CL games, but they score at home more than that suggests (xG 1.76 per game).

checks.team_news: Man City: Antoine Semenyo is the only confirmed absentee (knee, back near Christmas). Matheus Nunes (ankle, missed the 1-1 draw with Fulham) is fit per Maresca; he said other players have tiredness doubts and he will decide after training (Sports Mole). Napoli visit without 11 players (Yahoo Sports): injured Alisson Santos, Badiashile, Buongiorno, Di Lorenzo, Lobotka, Meret (GK), Neres, Vergara (thigh tear, 2+ months); suspended Rafa Marin; Marianucci and Favasuli not in the UEFA squad. Allegri is missing four of six centre-backs and a stand-in goalkeeper is needed.
checks.lineups: Not out yet (morning). Khel Now predicted City 4-2-3-1: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, O'Reilly; Fernandez, Anderson; Ndiaye, Foden, Doku; Haaland. Napoli 3-5-1-1: Contini; Beukema, Rrahmani, Marin; Politano, Anguissa, Gilmour, McTominay, Vergara; De Bruyne; Hojlund (this list includes Marin and Vergara, who are out per Yahoo, so it is unreliable). Esteemed Kompany expects a strong City XI with any rotation later in the game. Maresca called the season a 65-game marathon and says he must manage workload. Official XIs not yet announced.
checks.rotation: City: previous league game a 1-1 draw with Fulham, next game at Arsenal on Sunday; Maresca talks of fatigue and workload, so a few changes are plausible but no heavy rotation is reported. Last CL game a 3-2 win at RB Leipzig (Haaland winner). Napoli: beat Torino 1-0 on Saturday; Allegri is downplaying this game and says the campaign will be decided against Club Brugge, Sabah and Viking, so he may also manage his squad. Napoli travel with a depleted squad.
checks.motivation: League-phase table (ESPN, 4 games each): City 7th, 9 pts (3W 0D 1L, +5), inside the top 8 but level on points with 8th-12th, so a win matters for direct last-16 entry. Napoli 27th, 3 pts (1W 3L, -5), outside the play-off places (top 24) and in need of points. City still need the result, so this is not a hard exclusion.
checks.form: City: winless in their last four Premier League games (1 win in the last 6 in all competitions per Esteemed Kompany), including the 1-1 draw with Fulham; two straight CL wins (3-2 at Leipzig). City have conceded 11 goals in four CL games. Napoli: lost 4-1 at Porto on matchday 4, only win 4-3 over Bodo/Glimt, beat Torino 1-0 on Saturday, 8th in Serie A. Both defences leak goals, which favours goals legs, but City's poor domestic run raises the draw risk.
checks.h2h: City won 2-0 in the 2025-26 league phase and have won their last three European meetings with Napoli (beIN Sports); Khel Now lists the last five as City 3 wins, Napoli 1 win, 1 draw. Kevin De Bruyne returns to the Etihad with Napoli. Style: City dominate possession against a 3-5-2/3-5-1-1 low-block side; the draw is the usual route to failure.
checks.odds: Polymarket (event 1326285, volume about $26.8k, thin): City win 0.745, draw 0.145, Napoli 0.095. Polymarket price 24h ago 0.765, now 0.745 (-2.6% relative, under the 3% threshold; the drop was a single step at about 09-10 hours ago and the price has been flat since). DraftKings via ESPN: home 1.29, draw 6.0, away 8.5, de-vigged 73.1/15.8/11.1; it agrees with Polymarket within 2 points. DraftKings opening was 1.24/6.0/9.5 (home de-vigged about 74.8%, now 73.1%, about -2.3% relative), a small drift that Maresca's fatigue and rotation comments plausibly explain. DraftKings total line 3.5. Khel Now lists Over 3.5 goals at 10/11 (bet365).
checks.models: World Football Elo data not provided for this club game. Foresportia (not bookmaker-based) rates City 1557 vs Napoli 1448 and projects 50.1% City / 28.3% draw / 21.6% Napoli; Sports Mole's model gives 54.65% / 21.83% / 23.52%. Both models are well below the 73-75% market, which is a reason to stay cautious and to lower p; they are weak models and do not account for Napoli's 11 absences.
checks.venue_weather: Etihad Stadium, Manchester (City's normal home ground, ESPN scoreboard confirms the fixture on 2026-11-24 20:00 UTC, UEFA Champions League league phase matchday 5). Referee Istvan Kovacs (Romania). No weather or pitch problem reported; no weather figures found.

games.reason: Fixture verified on ESPN. No hard exclusion: Maresca was appointed in June 2026 and Allegri in June 2026, so there has been no coach change in the last 7 days; City still need points for a top-8 finish while Napoli, 27th, need points too; no confirmed heavy rotation; not a derby; normal venue. City are strong favourites against a Napoli side missing 11 players including its first-choice goalkeeper and four centre-backs, and the second price (DraftKings 73.1%) agrees with Polymarket. Confidence is medium and not high because lineups are unconfirmed, City are in poor domestic form (winless in four league games), Maresca flags fatigue, Napoli's first-choice XI is not what the predictions assumed, and bookmaker-free models rate City far lower than the market. p is lowered from the market toward the draw. Set to low when merged: the two bookmaker-free models sit about 20 points under the market, a doubt the 5-point limit on p cannot reflect (as for Paris FC on 22 Nov), with City winless in four league games and rotation possible before Arsenal.
games.main_risk: A draw or one-goal game: City in poor league form (winless in four league games, one win in six), fatigue-driven rotation with Arsenal on Sunday, and a deep-sitting Napoli that Allegri may set up to take a point. A 1-0 or 2-0 City win would also fail the goals legs.

checks.team_news: Leipzig (coach Martin Demichelis): centre-back Castello Lukeba out with a bruised knee and Maxime Esteve is tipped to replace him next to Willi Orban (RBL press conference 23 Nov via bulinews/Yahoo, OneFootball). Marc Guiu (hamstring) and Assan Ouedraogo (shoulder) also out; sources disagree on whether Zingerle is suspended or just not in the CL squad. Lens: Bulatovic (neck), Edouard (groin), Gradit, Nawrocki (knee) out and Ivanovic (concussion) doubtful, with Aguilar a muscle doubt; Jourdren suspended (tufutbolero, OneFootball). Lens fans are banned from this away game after flares at Club Brugge. No Lens press-conference quotes found.
checks.lineups: Not out yet; the official XI comes 60 minutes before kick-off (bundesliga.com). Squawka predicts Leipzig in a 4-3-3 and Lens in a 3-4-2-1 with Thauvin the main threat. OneFootball tips Esteve with Orban in Leipzig's defence. No confirmed XI, so the lineups check cannot be called clean.
checks.rotation: No sign of rotation at Leipzig, who play at home and are not yet through. I could not find Leipzig's next league fixture or any Demichelis remark on rotation. Lens drew 1-1 at Toulouse at the weekend, lost 1-2 to Marseille the week before, and travel to Germany.
checks.motivation: Both sides sit on 3 points from 4 games (1 win, 3 losses each), Leipzig on goal difference -6 and Lens on -12. Neither has secured anything, so this is not a hard exclusion. Both need points for the top 24; Demichelis said Lens need the three points as well.
checks.form: Leipzig scored five goals in each of their last two games (form LWWWL) and have won every home game this season except a 2-3 loss to Man City. They lost 1-4 to Real Madrid in this competition. Lens form is WLWLL: 1-9 at home to Como, 0-3 at Club Brugge, 1-2 vs Marseille, 1-1 at Toulouse; they have lost their last three European games, are 11th in Ligue 1, and have won 1 of 13 away league games. No xG found.
checks.h2h: No previous competitive meeting. Lens won a friendly 2-1 in August 2025 (OneFootball). The Lens coach was changed: Cahuzac was sacked around 10-12 Nov and Didier Digard was appointed on 13 Nov, 11 days before kick-off, so this is a soft risk outside the 7-day hard rule. Digard's first match was the 1-1 draw at Toulouse.
checks.odds: Polymarket live: home 71.5%, draw 16.5%, away 12.5%; the event had about $11.7k volume and $491k liquidity, so the market is liquid. 24h move: 70.5% to 71.5% (+1.4%), so the favourite did not fall. DraftKings via ESPN: 1.37/5.75/7.00, de-vigged 69.7/16.6/13.7; it opened at 1.43/5.25/5.50, so the favourite has shortened. Bet365 per kickoff.co.uk: 1.36/5.25/7.50. The independent prices are within 2 points of Polymarket.
checks.models: ClubElo: Leipzig 1841 (26th), Lens 1777 (55th), a gap of 64 points before home advantage, consistent with about 70% for the home side. Squawka model: 73/15/12. KickOff algorithm: 71/16/13, with 2.8 goals for Leipzig and 1.2 for Lens.
checks.venue_weather: Red Bull Arena, Leipzig, 21:00 CET (20:00 UTC), a normal home venue. I did not find a weather report for the night, so I flag no extreme weather.

games.reason: Leipzig are about 70% across Polymarket, DraftKings, Bet365 and the models, there is no hard exclusion, and the favourite's price rose over 24h. Lens come with a coach change 11 days ago, a heavy injury list, and a 1-9 and a 0-3 heavy defeat in this competition. Medium rather than high because no XI is confirmed and Lukeba is out, and because Leipzig have conceded 3 to City and 4 to Real. Draw chance about 17%, under the 25% limit.
games.main_risk: A draw or upset: a Leipzig defence without Lukeba, which has leaked goals against good teams, against a Lens side with a new coach that may play with nothing to lose. A big Leipzig win by 4+ would hurt the Lens +3.5 handicap, and Leipzig's goal tally depends on which XI starts.

checks.team_news: Arsenal: GK David Raya out (shoulder, sustained vs Newcastle; Arteta Monday: 'not fit for tomorrow, doesn't look too serious', no surgery, more tests Tuesday), Kepa Arrizabalaga the likely replacement; Bukayo Saka out (quad, not back until December per reports); Martin Zubimendi out (hamstring, several weeks); William Saliba back in training but Arteta will ease him in; Max Dowman available after a domestic suspension. Dortmund: coach Niko Kovac said Monday that Serhou Guirassy (thigh/hamstring) and Carney Chukwuemeka are fit and in the squad, starting 'we'll see tomorrow' (bvbwld.de, Sky Germany); out: Emre Can (ACL), Giannis Konstantelias (ACL), Samuele Inacio, Mussa Kaba (Sports Mole, Racing Post). Ethan Nwaneri (Arsenal loanee) is eligible for Dortmund. No suspensions found for the main XI.
checks.lineups: No official XIs yet (kick-off 20:00 UTC). Sports Mole predicted Arsenal: Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Gyokeres. Racing Post predicted 4-2-3-1: Arrizabalaga; White, Saliba, Mosquera, Hincapie; Rice, Lewis-Skelly; Madueke, Merino, Tzolis; Gyokeres. The two outlets disagree on the back line and attacking midfield, so the XI is uncertain. Dortmund predicted 3-4-2-1 (Kobel; Schlotterbeck, Anton, Bensebaini; Ryerson, Nmecha/Veerman, Bellingham, Svensson; Beier/Karetsas; Silva), with Guirassy possibly starting up front.
checks.rotation: Arsenal drew 2-2 at Newcastle on Saturday and play Manchester City at home on Sunday. Arteta said the squad has been rotated a lot ('they are all starters') and Racing Post says his selection is uncertain ahead of City. Lewis-Skelly, Tzolis, Merino and Gyokeres are likely to start after coming off the bench at Newcastle, so I expect a few changes, not a heavily rotated side. Not confirmed, so this is a soft risk. Dortmund are top of the Bundesliga and travelled to London; no heavy rotation reported.
checks.motivation: ESPN standings before the game (4 games each): Arsenal 3rd on 10 pts (+5), PSG and Real Madrid 12, Como 9 on +13. Dortmund 12th on 9 pts (+2), i.e. in the play-off zone just outside the top 8 (Liverpool 8th on 9 pts, +4). Arsenal are not yet safe in the top 8 and Dortmund need the result to climb, so neither side has secured its aim and there is no hard exclusion. A win would nearly settle Arsenal's top-8 place. Arteta says the open league-phase format means every game needs urgency.
checks.form: Arsenal, last 6 all competitions (Sports Mole): W L W W W D. League phase: W Napoli, W Lille, D 2-2 Bayern, W Slavia Prague. Won three before the break by one goal each (Liverpool, Slavia, Hull), then drew 2-2 at Newcastle; scored in 17 of 18 games this season and conceded in 2 of the last 3 (Covers). 16 games unbeaten in the league phase. Dortmund: W W D W W W; 3 wins and a 2-2 draw at Bayern in their first four Champions League games (Racing Post); top of the Bundesliga with 7 wins and 3 draws from 10, lost only 1 of their last 16, both teams scored in 4 of their last 5. Dortmund are in good form and Kobel plus Guirassy's return make them dangerous. No xG data found.
checks.h2h: Arsenal 4 wins, Dortmund 3 (Sports Mole); the last competitive meeting was a 2-0 Arsenal win in November 2014. Arteta notes Dortmund beat Arsenal in pre-season last summer (friendly, little weight). Not a derby or rivalry. Style: Arsenal are well drilled and win tight, low-margin games; Dortmund (3-4-2-1) score regularly, so a draw or Dortmund goal is the realistic failure.
checks.odds: Polymarket (event 1326293, volume about $190k, liquid): home 0.685 / draw 0.195 / away 0.125 live. 24h move for Arsenal: 0.705 to 0.685 (-2.8% relative, under the 3% line). The drift came at about 17:00 UTC Monday and 05:00 UTC Tuesday, which fits the Raya-out news and the Guirassy/Chukwuemeka fitness reports. DraftKings via ESPN: 1.44 / 4.60 / 7.00 (opening 1.40 / 4.70 / 7.00), de-vigged 0.658 / 0.207 / 0.136; its home price lengthened about 2.8% since opening, again explained by the news. bet365 (Racing Post): 4-11 / 4-1 / 7-1, which is about 0.69 / 0.19 / 0.12 once de-vigged (draw taken at 4-1, quoted on the page). Kalshi (Covers): Arsenal 71%, draw 19%, Dortmund 11%. Independent prices sit within about 3 points of Polymarket, so they agree. Total 2.5 line at DraftKings; Kalshi Over 2.5 at 58%.
checks.models: Opta supercomputer as reported in a preview (canadasportsbetting.ca snippet): Arsenal 65.2%, draw 19%, Dortmund 15.8%, about 3 points below the market for Arsenal.
